Model card: CiteNet: a legal-citation checker whose weights were written by hand A 397,250-parameter network (13,871 nonzero) that flags legal citations that cannot exist: an invented reporter series ( , ), a court the reporter never prints ( ), a state the regional reporter doesn't cover, or a year that doesn't fit the volume ( ; vol 912 is from 2018). **No training.** Claude (Anthropic) wrote : the reporters and their real series, which courts each reporter prints, the West regional map, and approximate volume→year timelines. It also wrote , which compiles each entry into specific weights: - a conv filter that fires only when the characters spell - digit decoders with weight k·10^i on digit k - a shared ReLU "volume thermometer" that every volume→year curve reads from - AND gates like Every nonzero weight has a name, and there was no gradient step. Results (LePhantomCite, held-out eval split, citation level) ai-law-society-lab/Legal_Phantom_Citation (Liu, Stammbach & Henderson 2026, CC BY 4.0). The network was designed using only the split. was scored once with frozen weights. | | phantom citations caught | real citations flagged | |---|---|---| | v1.0, first and only blind run | 31 / 31 | 3 / 983 | | v1.5 (this release; later fixes were not blind) | 31 / 31 | 1 / 983 | - **The remaining flag** is . A.2d never prints D.C. Circuit opinions, so it is likely an error in the source brief. - **Out of scope:** other hallucination types (case-name mismatch, wrong pincite, misquote) need the case text.
